title: Distribution of the Radius of Gyration for an ISAW
authors: Antony Lesage, Vincent Dahirel, Jean-Marc Victor, Maria Barbi
abstract: We aim at calculating an explicit expression for the finite-size probability distribution of the radius of gyration $R$ of an Interacting Self-Avoiding Walk (ISAW), as a function of chain length $N$ and monomer-monomer interaction energy $\varepsilon$. We first derive the explicit free energy expression for a non-interacting Self-Avoiding Walk, introducing a new natural scale variable $t = ρ^g$ expressed as a power of the density $ρ$. Then, thanks to a cumulant expansion approach introduced by Lhuillier, Victor and coworkers, we extend it to the interacting case, capturing both the coil-globule transition and finite-size corrections to scaling, including entropic and surface-energy contributions. The radius of gyration distribution determined by the new free energy expression is then compared, using Bayesian inference to estimate the model parameters, to results from extensive Monte Carlo simulations of three-dimensional ISAWs, showing excellent agreement except very close to the $Θ$-point, where finite chain lengths limit the accessible scaling regime. This validates our resulting free energy expression and allows us, as an application, to construct a phase diagram of the coil-globule transition.
summary: This work develops a theoretical framework to calculate the probability distribution of the radius of gyration for interacting polymer chains (ISAWs). By extending free energy calculations using cumulant expansions, the authors achieve an explicit formula that is validated against detailed Monte Carlo simulations. This allows them to map out the phase diagram governing the coil-globule transition in these polymeric systems.
main_problem: To derive an explicit, finite-size probability distribution for the radius of gyration ($R$) of an Interacting Self-Avoiding Walk (ISAW) as a function of chain length and interaction energy.
main_result: The derived free energy expression shows excellent agreement with extensive Monte Carlo simulations across various regimes, allowing for the construction of a phase diagram for the coil-globule transition.
method: The authors extend existing work using a cumulant expansion approach to derive the free energy, which is then compared against numerical simulation results via Bayesian inference.
model_or_system: The system modeled is an Interacting Self-Avoiding Walk (ISAW) on a lattice, representing self-attracting linear homopolymers. The interactions are governed by monomer-monomer contact energy ($\epsilon$).
key_observables: Radius of gyration ($R$), the probability distribution $P(R\mid \varepsilon, N)$, and the mean radius of gyration $ ar{R}$.
important_parameters: Chain length ($N$), monomer-monomer interaction energy ($\epsilon$), and the critical temperature/point ($\Theta$-point).
main_assumptions: The derivation relies on extending free energy calculations from non-interacting SAWs using cumulant expansions, assuming analyticity in certain density variables.
figures_summary: Figures compare theoretical predictions (inferred free energy parameters) and histograms of $P(R^2|\epsilon, N)$ against Monte Carlo simulation results across different solvent conditions ($\epsilon$) and chain lengths ($N$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the SAW case, then extending it to ISAW using cumulant expansions. The core is the comparison of the resulting free energy expression with extensive MC simulations to validate the model and map out the phase diagram.
why_interesting: While focused on polymer physics, the rigorous application of scaling theories, critical phenomena analysis (coil-globule transition), and advanced statistical mechanics techniques for finite systems provides methodological insights applicable to analyzing complex many-body systems in AMO or quantum field theory contexts.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
